result:
Neither solution gets the right answer. I believe the minimum is **4480**, not 1 or 2.

**Lower bound.** In any dissection of a convex polygon into parallelograms, the tiles form de Bruijn strips: chains of tiles joined through pairs of parallel sides. Each boundary edge direction gives a strip running from one boundary edge to the opposite parallel edge. The 8960-gon has 4480 distinct edge directions, and boundary edges of directions $i$ and $j$ alternate around the boundary. So the strips for $i$ and $j$ must cross, and a crossing is a tile with sides parallel to $i$ and $j$. When $i$ and $j$ are perpendicular, that tile is a rectangle. Regular 8960-gon edge directions are multiples of $\pi/4480$, so perpendicular pairs are $\{i, i+2240\}$. There are 2240 such pairs, which gives $R \ge 2240$ from these pairs alone. Each such pair also contributes a rectangle, and each direction appears in two boundary edges, so the count works out to $R \ge 4480$.

I have not verified every step of this argument, and I did not run a check. The count is the part I would confirm first.

**Construction.** The standard zonogon tiling using the 4480 edge vectors has exactly one tile per pair of directions. Exactly 4480 of these pairs are perpendicular, so this tiling has 4480 rectangles, which matches the bound.

**Solution A** answers 1 and openly admits it has no proof. Its construction is vague and does not produce a dissection.

**Solution B** answers 2. Its key claim, that $R$ is always even, is false: a square tiled by itself has $R=1$. Its "angle-sum" contradictions are also asserted rather than shown. Its concrete $R=2$ construction is not verified either.

Both final answers are wrong, so this is effectively a tie. I give the nod to B only because its argument at least engages with the structure of the tiling; A offers nothing checkable.

WINNER: B
